text:
Dear Dr. Henderson,

Thank you for seeing this eleven-month-old boy for further evaluation. I have followed him since birth following a neonatal onset of convulsive episodes, which have been managed with levetiracetam. His family history is non-contributory, and his parents are healthy and non-consanguineous.

On examination, he demonstrates diffuse increased muscular tone throughout the axial and appendicular musculature. His cranial contour shows pronounced frontal bossing accompanied by midfacial retrusion, an upturned nasal tip with forward-tilted nostrils, infraorbital folds, and a noticeably shortened philtral groove. His ears are posteriorly rotated and low-lying, with markedly prominent, fleshy lobules. 

Skeletal survey reveals a progressive thoracolumbar spinal curvature, along with bilaterally hypoplastic first metacarpal bones and shortened distal phalanges of the digits. Forearm views were normal, with no evidence of synostosis between the radius and ulna. Abdominal imaging identified bilateral dilation of the renal collecting systems. On genital examination, his testes are descended, but he has an exceptionally diminutive phallus measuring under two centimeters stretched length. 

Neuroimaging previously demonstrated enlarged lateral ventricles without obstructing lesions. A recent endocrine workup was notable for a low serum free thyroxine concentration, though his thyroid-stimulating hormone, electrolyte panel, and complete blood counts were within normal limits. 

Given these complex multisystem findings, I would appreciate your expert clinical assessment and guidance regarding further diagnostic investigation.

Sincerely,
Dr. Marcus Alvarez, MD
